However, I'm not aware of an in-built way to define the signature threshold - it seems that the threshold can only be enforced by the verifier (i.e. check that the aggregated signature is valid for at least 2 of the 3 aggregated pubkeys) Will ETH2 have a way to define a signature threshold for accounts? Am I missing something and this is actually non-issue? you don't necessarily get more rewards but it is very straightforward to e.g. include attestations from the block at slot S-1 in your slot S and collect the proposer share for the attestations that would have been in both blocks there are a number of issues w/ having the proposer be known in advance and there is some research to make this "leader election" secret i can link you more info on ethresear.ch if you'd like validators in general should guard their identity by not associating real name/social media accounts with their public key, and hide their IP using a VPN at minimum, but preferably routing the whole setup through Tor. the more validators' (quasi-)identity and location are known, the more vulnerable the network becomes to sovereign-level attackers this includes first shuffling deposit funds through Tornado Cash or a privacy coin the first thing to be clear is that we use BLS signatures at the consensus layer for the purposes of validators and we won't necessarily use them at the user-level (when and where that comes about -- nothing is stopping a migration to "BLS accounts" but that likely falls under the account abstraction research that is ongoing along w/ the details of the eth1-eth2 merge which also has ongoing discussion 🙂 ) so then you can talk about threshold schemes for validators where there are several options like "secret shared validators" but i will also point out there are good reasons why the current consensus is to run "simple staking setups" until the software stack matures a bit more overall Ah, interesting - I didn't know that it wasn't intended for user accounts. excerpts.author: mtoda8639
excerpts.content:
Hey all, I have a question about m-of-n aggregated signature verification in ETH2 (apologies if this is not the correct channel for this type of question)

We use a 2-of-3 multi-signature scheme for our wallets and are working on our ETH2 implementation. It's pretty easy with BLS to aggregate 3 public keys, and similarly to aggregate the 2 signatures. However, I'm not aware of an in-built way to define the signature threshold - it seems that the threshold can only be enforced by the verifier (i.e. check that the aggregated signature is valid for at least 2 of the 3 aggregated pubkeys)

Will ETH2 have a way to define a signature threshold for accounts? Am I missing something and this is actually non-issue?

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: you don't necessarily get more rewards but it is very straightforward to e.g. include attestations from the block at slot S-1 in your slot S and collect the proposer share for the attestations that would have been in both blocks

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: there are a number of issues w/ having the proposer be known in advance and there is some research to make this "leader election" secret

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: i can link you more info on ethresear.ch if you'd like

excerpts.author: chaserxy
excerpts.content: validators in general should guard their identity by not associating real name/social media accounts with their public key, and hide their IP using a VPN at minimum, but preferably routing the whole setup through Tor.

excerpts.author: chaserxy
excerpts.content: the more validators' (quasi-)identity and location are known, the  more vulnerable the network becomes to sovereign-level attackers

excerpts.author: chaserxy
excerpts.content: this includes first shuffling deposit funds through Tornado Cash or a privacy coin

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content:
the first thing to be clear is that we use BLS signatures at the consensus layer for the purposes of validators and we won't necessarily use them at the user-level (when and where that comes about -- nothing is stopping a migration to "BLS accounts" but that likely falls under the account abstraction research that is ongoing along w/ the details of the eth1-eth2 merge which also has ongoing discussion 🙂 )

so then you can talk about threshold schemes for validators where there are several options like "secret shared validators" but i will also point out there are good reasons why the current consensus is to run "simple staking setups" until the software stack matures a bit more overall

excerpts.author: mtoda8639
excerpts.content: Ah, interesting - I didn't know that it wasn't intended for user accounts. We are currently working on implementation for the withdrawal key for validators, though - just want to make sure that our 3-aggregated-key withdrawal keys will be withdrawable with signatures from 2 of the keys when the time comes that they can withdraw

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: it is not not intended for user accounts

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: its more that the decision has not been made yet

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: my understanding is that you do the threshold set-up "off chain" so that the withdrawal credential is a commitment to the threshold public key and then any 2 of the 3 member signatures can be used to recreate a validating signature when it is time to withdraw

excerpts.author: mtoda8639
excerpts.content: Ah, OK - that would solve my issue. The BLS library we've been using (https://github.com/ChainSafe/bls) doesn't seem to have a way to specify an aggregated key's threshold. Maybe they have only planned for the n-of-n situation. I'll bring this up with them, in that case - Thank you!
